summary: Keep each GitHub observer's poll cursor in the polling member's plugin database, <state>/plugins/github/github.sqlite3, instead of in observer.observed claims that replicate to every member.

replay.detail: No claim is rewritten or replayed. Claims older builds wrote keep their cursor field and stay valid.

schema.detail: The claims database schema and its version are unchanged. New local file <state>/plugins/github/github.sqlite3 (PRAGMA user_version 1, one table observer_cursors keyed by observer subject, one row per observer this member polled), created on first start. It never syncs and is not in a backup. The daemon refuses to start when it cannot open the file or finds a newer version; deleting the file costs each repository observer one full read and delivers nothing twice.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes. No fleet barrier or coordinated upgrade: each member changes only its own writes.

compatibility.detail: Claim vocabulary (contract change C1): observer.observed no longer carries cursor; it keeps status, revision, changed and attempt. Only github.repository observers (observer/github/*) ever wrote one. The field stays in the claim registry (/v1/schema, st schema claims) as optional, because older members still write it. No client-v0 change. Mixed versions need no barrier. An older poller keeps writing cursors until it upgrades. An upgraded member with no row for an observer polls from the cursor in that observer's newest observer.observed claim, then keeps a row, so it adopts a claim's cursor once per plugin database. A member that takes over polling without a cursor (any build) reads every open item once: items whose facts equal the recorded ones deliver nothing, and it delivers only what changed since (an item opened meanwhile, a pull request at a new ready head). An older member reads the observer's folded actual state, which keeps the last cursor an older build wrote, an earlier point than the new poller's; taking over, it reads again from there and likewise delivers only what changed. An observer whose poll cannot keep its cursor is degraded with error code github-plugin-database.

downtime.detail: No startup migration beyond creating the plugin file. The first poll after upgrade continues from the cursor in the observer's newest claim.

manual.detail: No operator action on upgrade. If the daemon refuses to start naming github.sqlite3, delete <state>/plugins/github/github.sqlite3 and start it again.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to an older build is supported. The older build reads the last cursor an older build wrote, kept in the observer's folded actual state, or none when the observer was first polled by this build; it reads again from that point (a full read without one) within the github-admission hourly budget and delivers only what changed since the recorded facts. Older builds ignore the plugin file, which may be deleted.
